questions.q: Which four symptoms does Rumelt use to describe bad strategy?
a: Fluff, avoiding the challenge, goals as strategy and bad objectives
Poor timing, weak branding, high costs and slow hiring
Too many leaders, unclear values, low morale and bad data
Copying rivals, cutting prices, overspending and drifting
questions.why: Lesson 1 lists fluff, failure to face the challenge, mistaking goals for strategy and bad objectives.

questions.q: Why is growing revenue by 20 percent not a strategy?
a: It states a wish, not how you will achieve it
It is too modest a target for most firms
It cannot be measured accurately
It belongs in marketing, not strategy
questions.why: Lesson 1 says strategy is about the how, not the what.

questions.q: What are the three parts of a good strategy's kernel?
a: Diagnosis, guiding policy and coherent actions
Vision, mission and values
Analysis, budget and timeline
Goal, metric and review
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the kernel is a diagnosis, an overarching policy and a set of coherent actions.

questions.q: In the Tesla example, what was the guiding policy?
a: Build electric cars people actually want, starting with one model
Cut prices until electric cars outsell gas cars
License battery technology to other automakers
Focus on cheap cars for city drivers first
questions.why: Lesson 2 says Tesla decided to make desirable EVs, starting with the Roadster.

questions.q: How did Nvidia carry out its strategy after choosing 3D chips?
a: It set up three teams to release new chips every six months
It bought smaller chip firms to expand quickly
It cut prices to undercut established rivals
It focused on software instead of hardware
questions.why: Lesson 3 describes overlapping teams built to hit a six-month release cycle.
